newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hitachi to sell high-capacity FRAM chips.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi to sell high-capacity FRAM chips.

text.p: Electronics giant Hitachi Ltd said Monday it has developed high-capacity ferroelectric random access memory (FRAM) chips with 256 kilobits of memory and will begin marketing them in Japan in December.
The product -- which Hitachi said was the world's first 256 kilobit FRAM chip -- was jointly developed with semiconductor maker Ramtron International Corp. of the United States.
FRAM chips can retain memory without electricity and the memory can be rewritten up to one trillion times.
Currently, conventional FRAM chips can store 14 kilobits, 16 kilobits and 64 kilobits of memory.
Hitachi said that FRAM chips can be used in a wide range of products, including cellular phones, personal information organisers, pagers and train passes that can be automatically read by a sensor.

Hitachi and Ramtron agreed to develop the high-density FRAM devices jointly in 1994. Ramtron was to provide ferroelectric technology and Hitachi was to contribute its mass production know-how, the statement said.
